newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit makes sharp recovery on Mahathir's comment.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit makes sharp recovery on Mahathir's comment.

text.p: The ringgit made a sharp recovery after Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said there was no need to weaken the Malaysian unit, dealers said on Tuesday.
They said the directionless Malaysian unit defied general market trend of a strong dollar to move up nearly 50 points within minutes of the Prime Minister's statement.
At 0400 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5017/27 per dollar against 2.5060/70 an hour earlier.
"This is purely a reaction to Mahathir's comments. Ringgit should improve more in the next few minutes," said the head of regional currencies at a European bank in Singapore.
"It should recover to around 2.50 level before falling back because the big dollar is still very firm," he said.
Mahathir told reporters at an energy conference that he didn't "see the need to lower the ringgit".
"I don't like the manipulation of the currency to the point where we lose control," he said when asked if the country would let the currency weaken.
Earlier, the ringgit was trading in a range, but was under pressure from a surging dollar.
"The market was waiting for some excuse to push down dollar/ringgit," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
